thread:
maya: FYI customer (org: acme_health) escalated — when using JSON streaming mode their ingestion fails with 'Unexpected end of JSON input'. Req id: req_0a1b2c3d. Happens intermittently on long responses (~2k+ tokens).
ryan: Can you paste their curl / client snippet? Any proxies in path? :thinking_face:
maya: They go client -> CloudFront -> our hosted API. Provided curl: `curl -i -N -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate?mode=json' --data-binary @prompt.json`
logs-bot: [trace] req=req_0a1b2c3d events: 2026-01-12T15:02:12Z send chunk size=1536; 2026-01-12T15:02:14Z keepalive; 2026-01-12T15:02:14Z downstream FIN; 2026-01-12T15:02:14Z stream aborted mid-object
maya: Customer parser error shows arrays missing trailing ']' or objects missing '}'. They say it only happens with streaming; non-streaming full-response JSON works fine.
deepa: Repro notes: our runtime emits top-level array elements as individual chunks. If downstream connection is closed before we send final ']', client sees incomplete array. I reproduced by killing client socket at random chunk boundaries — parser error occurs.
ryan: Downstream FIN at keepalive timepoints suggests intermediary (CloudFront) idle timeout or client-side connection recycling. CloudFront default idle timeout can tear connections during long-lived SSE connections.
maya: Customer insists client didn't close, so likely CloudFront or a network hop. They want a production-safe mitigation — ingestion pipeline is failing and they see billing/alerts.
deepa: Short-term options: 1) ask customer to use `stream=false` to get atomic whole JSON (quick fix), 2) provide a client-side tolerant parser snippet (heuristic) to attempt to recover, 3) server-side postprocess to emit a safe terminator on downstream close (needs careful review).
ryan: We should avoid silent fixes that mask real truncation. But for an emergency mitigation we can enable a feature flag that attempts to append a closing token when it detects downstream close during streaming for a specific org. I'll provision flag `streaming-json-postprocess` for acme_health.
maya: Customer wants the flag now. Can we also suggest infra changes (CloudFront idle extension) while we monitor?
deepa: Draft client heuristics (for customer only):
Node (naive):
```js
const res = await fetch(url, opts);
let body = '';
for await (const chunk of res.body) body += chunk.toString();
try { JSON.parse(body); } catch (e) {
  // best-effort salvage
  const trimmed = body.trim();
  if (trimmed.endsWith(',')) body = trimmed.slice(0, -1) + ']';
  else if (!trimmed.endsWith('}') && trimmed.includes('{')) body += '}';
  JSON.parse(body);
}
```
Python (naive):
```py
b = resp.content.decode()
try:
    json.loads(b)
except json.JSONDecodeError:
    tb = b.strip()
    if tb.endswith(','):
        tb = tb[:-1] + ']'
    elif not tb.endswith('}') and '{' in tb:
        tb = tb + '}'
    json.loads(tb)
```
maya: We'll share the heuristics but mark as temporary and risky.
ryan: I'm going to enable the flag for acme_health for 48h and monitor error rate. I won't enable broadly without engineering review.
deepa: I'll open internal ticket MT-7892: "streaming-json: safe terminator emit on downstream close + tests for chunk boundary atomicity". Also add tests for CloudFront-style mid-connection close.
deepa: Two extra notes: 1) we should log downstream close reason/codes more verbosely (FIN vs RST vs proxy 503), 2) consider grouping tokens so we don't cut inside object fields when possible.
maya: deploy-bot: please confirm flag rollout and who enabled it.
deploy-bot: Rollout started: feature flag `streaming-json-postprocess` enabled for org:acme_health by ryan at 3337780100
maya: Thanks — I'll tell the customer we enabled a temporary server-side postprocess + recommend they try `stream=false` for immediate stability and request CloudFront idle-extension from infra. Will monitor. :thumbsup:
ryan: I'll watch logs for req_0a1b2c3d and similar IDs.
deepa: Filed MT-7892 and added unit/integration test notes.
maya: Closing loop after 48h monitor; will update thread.
